note: The thin shared reference the two agents construct for the RAN/core transport seam. Identity-only entries for the seam concepts, plus the native-only concepts named apart so the 'session' trap binds correctly. No entry for opaque vendor tags. Crucially, radio-session and core-session are DISTINCT entries, so two concepts both labelled 'session' bind apart rather than merging.

entries.label: user-plane transport
entries.definition: The user-plane transport connection carrying subscriber traffic between a cell site and the core user-plane function.

entries.label: transport demarcation
entries.definition: The point where the user-plane transport is handed off between the access and the core; one co-owned demarcation.
entries.example: the site-441 hand-off toward the core

entries.label: transport QoS marking
entries.definition: The DiffServ marking honoured on user-plane packets across the transport, mapped from the session's QoS.

entries.label: transport capacity
entries.definition: The committed transport capacity available to subscriber traffic on the connection.
entries.example: 8 Gbit/s committed at the busy hour

entries.label: transport MTU
entries.definition: The MTU on the transport, sized to carry encapsulated user-plane packets without fragmentation.

entries.label: radio cell
entries.definition: A coverage area served over the air interface; a radio-internal concept with no transport counterpart.

entries.label: RRC session
entries.definition: A device's radio-resource-control connection state on the air interface; a radio-internal 'session', unrelated to a core data session.
entries.example: the RRC-connected session for a handset in cell 441-A

entries.label: QoS flow
entries.definition: The finest granularity of QoS within a core data session; a core-internal concept with no transport counterpart.

entries.label: PDU session
entries.definition: A subscriber's end-to-end data connection through the core to a data network; a core-internal 'session', unrelated to a radio connection.
